builder_plan.scenario: Your coding assistant makes changes that still need substantial repair before merging.
builder_plan.change: Try the technique on held-out issues from a repository with reliable tests.
builder_plan.baseline: The same coding agent, repository snapshot, tools, and token budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct patches, regression failures, human repair time, and total cost per accepted change.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Spec-Driven PBT: Deriving Semantic Invariants from Code Specifications for Agentic Property-based Testing
summary: It replaces deriving test invariants solely from the implementation by first extracting natural-language invariants from the product specification and then using the code to translate them into executable property tests. The cost is an additional specification-analysis step plus dependence on a sufficiently detailed specification and an LLM agent pipeline for test generation. It can fail when specifications are incomplete or ambiguous, when generated properties are not executable or faithful, and when implementation-robustness bugs remain better covered by code-driven testing.
rationale: The method is directly relevant to teams shipping agent-generated code, but its practical value depends on specification quality and validation against the reader's own codebase and review workflow.
technique: Specification-driven property-based testing for agent-written code

claims.statement: It replaces deriving test invariants solely from the implementation by first extracting natural-language invariants from the product specification and then using the code to translate them into executable property tests. The cost is an additional specification-analysis step plus dependence on a sufficiently detailed specification and an LLM agent pipeline for test generation. It can fail when specifications are incomplete or ambiguous, when generated properties are not executable or faithful, and when implementation-robustness bugs remain better covered by code-driven testing.

Across 25 ViBench applications, Spec-Driven PBT finds a novel set of bugs that Code-driven PBT misses while writing 2.4x fewer property tests; nearly 60% of 169 total bugs are found by only one approach.
